solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Call for silence, one at crease taking first off break (7)

indicators.note: to take something off is to remove it, and 'first' names what goes: the opening letter of the word before

blocks.note: the one at the crease in cricket is the BATTER; without its first letter, ATTER

annotation.surface: A cricket scene: the umpire calls for hush while the batter at the crease faces a ball that breaks off the pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line where the batter stands. 'Break' looks like a spin bowler's turn off the pitch but is a plain verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to shatter something is to break it into many pieces.

entries.clue: Muscle toners just the thing to plug small delivery company (3-3)

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so the piece before it is pushed inside the pieces after it

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: Someone recommends a gym product and plugs a little courier firm in the same breath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plug' pretends to mean advertise, which suits the talk of products; it means stop up a gap.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: sit-ups are exercises that tone the stomach muscles.

entries.clue: Periods before noon ignoring husband’s love affairs (6)

indicators.note: to ignore someone is to leave them out, so the husband's letter is left out

blocks.note: AM HOURS, the hours before midday

annotation.surface: A spouse's morning trysts go on while the husband is kept in the dark.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s in 'husband’s' stands for 'husband is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing from French: amours are love affairs, usually secret or illicit ones.

entries.clue: Is boyfriend, one dividing white powder, bringing luck? (10)

indicators.note: a thing that divides another sits in its middle, splitting it in two

blocks.note: talcum powder; ISMANI splits it TAL…C

annotation.surface: A slightly sinister question about a boyfriend cutting lines of white powder.
annotation.walkthrough: The white powder looks like something illicit; it is only talc.
annotation.definitionFit: Derived from the noun: a talisman is a lucky charm, so talismanic describes whatever brings luck.

entries.clue: Old-style railway system having run for miles (5)

indicators.note: 'for' means in place of, so R (run) stands where M (miles) was

blocks.note: an underground railway, as in Paris
R = run, as on a cricket scorecard, replaces M = miles

annotation.surface: An old-fashioned railway line with a very long run.
annotation.walkthrough: R and M are standard abbreviations for run and miles; the surface makes 'run for miles' sound like the length of the line.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: retro describes a deliberately old style, like retro furniture.

entries.clue: Expert in the deep and superficial? (7)

blocks.note: an ace = an expert, one who is in the surf

annotation.surface: A riddle about a deep-sea expert who turns out to be shallow.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'Expert in the deep' as a champion surfer: the ace belongs in the surf, and the question mark flags that stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective use: a surface wound or surface charm is superficial, only skin-deep.

entries.clue: Tiny suspicion wrong steering device delivered (9)

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so the words are spoken out loud

blocks.note: sin = wrong, tiller = a boat's steering device

annotation.surface: A faint doubt that a faulty steering part was sent out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' looks like shipping; it means spoken. In non-rhotic British speech TILLER ends like -LLA, so SIN TILLER gives SCINTILLA.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition that leans on usage: a scintilla is the tiniest trace, most often in 'not a scintilla of suspicion'.

entries.clue: Opportunity offered by open area to the north (4)

indicators.note: in a down answer, heading north means reading from bottom to top

annotation.surface: A chance arises thanks to open country lying north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Room' in the sense of scope, as in 'room for improvement'.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: room can mean scope or opportunity, as in 'room for manoeuvre'.

entries.clue: American idealist hasn’t name like Basil perhaps (8)

indicators.note: the idealist 'has not' a name, so N is missing from it

blocks.note: N = name, removed from ROMANTIC to leave ROMATIC

annotation.surface: A dreamy American lacks a name, rather like Basil Fawlty or some other Basil.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital B dresses the herb basil as a man's name, hinting at a person; it is the plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: basil is one of many aromatic herbs, which 'perhaps' signals.

entries.clue: Proceeds with scholarship, having wasted fifty seconds (8)

indicators.note: what is wasted is thrown away, so the fifty is lost from the word

blocks.note: L = fifty, the Roman numeral, dropped
S = seconds, added at the end

annotation.surface: Someone takes the money from a scholarship, having squandered fifty seconds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' is the noun (money taken in), not the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for money coming in: the proceeds of a sale are its earnings.

entries.clue: Provocative person goes for a walk naked (5)

indicators.note: someone naked is stripped of their covering, so the word loses its outer letters

annotation.surface: Someone out to shock takes a nude stroll.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a streaker; 'naked' is the instruction to strip the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An internet sense: a troll posts deliberately inflammatory messages to provoke others.

entries.clue: Standard business with bad look after brief stumble (9)

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the stumble loses its last letter
the business and the look are placed after the stumble

annotation.surface: An ordinary firm gives someone a dirty look after they trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a flag here, not ordinary. To lour (or lower) is to frown darkly.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a standard is a flag, and a tricolour such as the French flag is one kind.

entries.clue: Cycling speedway possibly opening in city (10)

indicators.note: cycling goes round in a loop, so the first letter comes round to the end

blocks.note: speedway (motorbike racing) is a SPORT; cycled, S moves to the end

annotation.surface: Cycling and speedway racing might open in a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like another sport beside speedway; it is the instruction. Portsmouth is a naval city on England's south coast.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Portsmouth is a city on the south coast of England.

entries.clue: Long pithy comment abridged (4)

indicators.note: an abridged book is shortened, so the word loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A remark meant to be pithy runs long and has to be cut.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts pithy with long, which hides that 'Long' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A fashion sense: maxi describes a garment reaching the ankles, like a maxi dress.

entries.clue: Stomach queasy digesting first pair of strawberries and jam (10)

indicators.note: what you digest is taken inside you, so the stomach and queasy pieces take ST in
the first two letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: can't stomach it = can't stand it

annotation.surface: An upset stomach from eating strawberries and jam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' is a verb (tolerate), and 'jam' is traffic, not preserve.
annotation.definitionFit: A traffic sense: a jam is a standstill, where nothing can move.

entries.clue: Are riots accompanying session taking place very disruptive? (3-9)

indicators.note: letters that riot run wild and end up in a new order
to accompany is to go alongside, so the two parts are placed side by side
a thing taking another holds it inside, so SITTING takes in PL

blocks.note: PL = place, as in street names; inside SITTING gives S…PL…ITTING

annotation.surface: A question whether rioting during a sitting of parliament would be disruptive.
annotation.walkthrough: Pl. is the address abbreviation for Place. The definition leans on noise so loud it disrupts everything nearby.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose, figurative fit: an ear-splitting din is loud enough to disrupt whatever is going on.

entries.clue: Knowing the story, Charlie is hosting centrepiece of tour (9)

indicators.note: a host has guests inside the house, so IS holds the tour's centre
the centre of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: a saga is a long story
used as it stands, around OU
the middle two letters of TOUR

annotation.surface: Charlie knows the tale and is hosting the highlight of a tour.
annotation.walkthrough: TOUR has four letters, so its centre is two letters rather than one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sagacious person is wise and knowing.

entries.clue: Worries of a soldier over condition beginning to end (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first pieces sit over (above) the next
the word's beginning is sent to its end

blocks.note: STATE = condition; its S moves to the end

annotation.surface: A soldier fretting about his state from start to finish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worries' is a verb here, as in 'it agitates him', not a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: whatever agitates you worries and unsettles you.

entries.clue: Forest, club country supports (8)

indicators.note: a support holds something up from below, so in a down answer LAND goes under WOOD

blocks.note: a wood is a golf club

annotation.surface: Nottingham Forest are a football club that the whole country supports.
annotation.walkthrough: Forest reads as Nottingham Forest, the English football club; the comma cuts it off as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a forest is a large area of woodland.

entries.clue: Temporary difficulties using blades to cut good French loaves (7,5)

annotation.surface: Knife trouble slicing a good French loaf.
annotation.walkthrough: The blades are oar blades, not knives. The pieces simply follow on: G, then the rowing, then the loaves.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: growing pains are the passing problems of something new or expanding.

entries.clue: It could hinder dropping off posh car rentals regularly scratched inside (3,3)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter
letters scratched into a car are scored on it, so they go inside the car's letters

blocks.note: the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of RENTALS, inside J…AG

annotation.surface: A posh hire car keeps getting keyed on the inside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' looks like returning the rental car; it means falling asleep.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: jet lag upsets the body clock, which makes it hard to fall asleep.

entries.clue: Sailor on base wearing ship’s goggles (6)

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits on top of the next
clothes wrap the wearer, so the ship's letters wrap round the rest

blocks.note: e, the base of natural logarithms
SS = steamship, split S…S around TARE

annotation.surface: A sailor at a naval base wears the ship's protective goggles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goggles' is a verb: he goggles, with eyes wide open.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to goggle is to gaze with wide eyes.

entries.clue: Direction of United discussed, … (4)

indicators.note: something discussed is talked about, so the word is heard, not seen

annotation.surface: Talk about the direction a football club called United is heading, continued in the next clue.
annotation.walkthrough: United looks like a football club; it simply means joined. The dots run the sense on into 22 across.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the tide of opinion is the direction it is flowing.

entries.clue: … panel faced with clubs inhibited by painful record? (5,5)

indicators.note: held in check by, so placed inside the painful word
a face is at the front, so the panel has the other piece before it

blocks.note: a sheet (of glass, metal) is a panel

annotation.surface: A club's board is faced with a painful run of results.
annotation.walkthrough: The dots make 21 and 22 one surface about United's bad run of form.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a score sheet is where a game's results are recorded.

entries.clue: What about dividing strong drink to bring about sleep? (5)

indicators.note: as in turning about, so EH is turned round
a thing dividing another sits in its middle, splitting it

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a stiff rum will help them nod off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sleep' is the gritty stuff in the eyes on waking, not slumber.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: the crust found in the eyes on waking is called sleep, and it is dried rheum.

entries.clue: For the audience I intend to rock out at sea (4)

indicators.note: an audience listens, so what follows is heard rather than read

annotation.surface: A performer announces to the crowd that they mean to rock out on a cruise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock out' looks like loud music; it is a rock sticking out of the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a small island can be no more than a rock standing out of the sea.

entries.clue: Swap drills, wanting current model (9)

indicators.note: in the old sense of lacking, so the current is missing from the drills

annotation.surface: A workshop swaps its drills for an up-to-date model.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drills' is a verb (trains, as troops are drilled), and 'current' is the physics symbol I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: transposing two items means making them swap places.

entries.clue: Layabout in discount store covering head on being knocked back (5)

indicators.note: the store's head is covered up and hidden, so its first letter drops out
knocked backwards, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: LIDL, the budget supermarket chain, minus its head L
RE = on (concerning), as in memo headings

annotation.surface: A loafer in a cheap supermarket covers his head after being knocked over.
annotation.walkthrough: Lidl is a German discount supermarket found across Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an idler is someone who lazes about doing nothing.

entries.clue: The Blues, Rangers send a signal over drinks (7)

indicators.note: as in turned over, so the word runs backwards
a drinker takes liquid inside, so SAS takes the reversed word in

blocks.note: the SAS, special forces like the US Rangers, around DNES
to send is to transmit a signal

annotation.surface: Football fans: the Blues and Rangers exchange signals over a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The Blues and Rangers look like football teams (Chelsea, Glasgow Rangers). The SAS is the British Army's special forces regiment.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to have the blues is to feel low, so the blues is a name for sadness.

entries.clue: Runs down motorway and straightens up (7)

blocks.note: to align is to line up straight

annotation.surface: A driver races down the motorway and straightens the car up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runs down' means criticises, not drives down.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to run someone down is to speak badly of them, which is to malign them.
